title: Why does a trapezium have the area of a triangle?
description: A is the middle of the slanting side XY of a trapezium ZYXW, and the line ZA is carried on to meet WX extended at B. The two small triangles ZYA and BXA match, so swapping one for the other shows that the trapezium and triangle ZWB have the same area.
teaching_notes: One idea: two matching triangles have equal areas, so swapping one for the other keeps the area. Watch for students who think the triangle sticking out at B must be bigger.

source: Trapezium ZYXW with ZY parallel to WX, A the midpoint of XY, ZA extended meeting WX extended at B, show area ZYXW = area of triangle ZWB
video_script.why: The child has split a trapezium into pieces and added their areas and now swaps one piece for a matching piece to show two different shapes have equal area.
video_script.substitution: The book question gives no numbers, so the sides stay as letters.
video_script.anchor: the trapezium ZYXW of the book with the line ZA carried on to B
video_script.payoff_line: The trapezium and triangle Z W B have the same area.

final_answer.value: area of trapezium ZYXW = area of triangle ZWB
final_answer.spoken: the trapezium and triangle Z W B have the same area

maths_rules: ZY parallel to WX, A is the midpoint of XY, ZA extended meets WX extended at B
YA = XA because A is the midpoint of XY
angle ZAY = angle BAX, vertically opposite angles
angle ZYA = angle BXA, alternate angles because ZY is parallel to WB
triangle ZYA and triangle BXA match (two angles and the side between them), so they have equal area
trapezium ZYXW = ZAXW + triangle ZYA = ZAXW + triangle BXA = triangle ZWB
video_script.design: One trapezium ZYXW stays all video with ZA carried on to B. The two small triangles ZYA and BXA are shaded in the same colour, and the one at B is swapped in for the one at Y.

<bookmark mark='trap'/>The sides Z Y and W X are parallel.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Eigh is the middle of the side X Y.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Carry the line Z eigh on until it meets W X, extended, at B.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The trapezium and the big triangle Z W B look different. Do they have the same area?

narration: <bookmark mark='vert'/>When two lines cross, the opposite angles are equal. They are called vertically opposite angles.
<bookmark mark='alt'/>A line across two parallel lines makes angles on opposite sides of it.
<bookmark mark='equal'/>These are called alternate angles, and they are equal.

narration: <bookmark mark='vert'/>Step two, the lines Z B and X Y cross at eigh. The angles Z eigh Y and B eigh X are vertically opposite, so they are equal.
<bookmark mark='alt'/>Z Y is parallel to W B. The angles Z Y eigh and B X eigh are alternate angles, so they are equal.
